message.content:
**Order filled: BUY 40 AAPL @ limit $223.00 (filled at $223.00, ~$8,920 notional).**

**Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended 2024-09-28, filed 2024-11-01), this morning's feed, and the latest news, then bought 40 shares of AAPL at a $223.00 limit — about 0.1% above the broker's last quote of $222.70, so well within "close to market," and $8,920 notional, inside both the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps, with no cash withdrawn (account held $50,000 cash plus 100 MSFT). The fundamentals supported a buy: FY2024 total net sales of $391,035 million (up 2% YoY), operating income of $123,216 million, net income of $93,736 million, diluted EPS of $6.08, and operating cash flow of $118,254 million — with the net income/EPS decline driven by a disclosed one-time $10.2 billion net tax charge tied to the EU State Aid Decision rather than operating deterioration, as gross margin actually expanded to 46.2% and Services grew 13% to $96,169 million. The Q4 release confirmed revenue of $94.9 billion, up 6% YoY, and the feed/news flow was benign — headlines noted iPhone 16 supplier builds steady into December, analysts holding holiday-quarter estimates unchanged, and shares "little changed" around $222 — so there was no negative catalyst to override the mandate. I sized the position modestly (40 shares) given the stock's flat intraday drift and the known overhangs flagged in the 10-K (Greater China net sales down 8% to $66,952 million, DOJ/EU antitrust and DMA exposure with potential fines up to 10% of worldwide net sales), leaving room to add on weakness within today's remaining budget.
